datasets.dataset_title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Public — western Pyrenean tile set

derived_artifacts.role: Terrain descriptor: extent, placement, intervals and attribution for the Atlas

geographic_extent.description: Six pinned 1°×1° tiles covering the western Pyrenees, the Béarn foothills and the Adour basin. CARTA acquires only the tiles the Béarn / Jurançon proof needs; no France-wide elevation ingestion exists.

datasets.geographic_meaning: Digital surface model of the western Pyrenees: bare ground plus vegetation canopy and buildings as observed by TanDEM-X between 2011 and 2015. It is physical relief context for CARTA Atlas. It is not evidence about vineyard land, planted parcels, growing conditions, ripening, drainage, climate or wine quality.

measurement.native_resolution: 1 arc-second grid (3600×3600 samples per 1° tile); ≈30 m north–south and ≈23 m east–west at 43°N
measurement.scale_limitations: Usable for regional relief reading down to roughly 1:50,000. It cannot resolve an individual vineyard parcel, a terrace, a wall or a row orientation, and as a surface model it carries tree canopy and building heights as if they were ground.
measurement.uncertainty: Per-tile absolute vertical accuracy LE90 between 1.741 m and 1.971 m (LE68 1.468–1.642 m) as reported by the Copernicus tile accuracy masks; the programme specification is LE90 < 4 m vertical and CE90 < 6 m horizontal.

datasets.publisher: Copernicus programme — European Union and ESA (data © DLR e.V. and Airbus Defence and Space GmbH)
datasets.refresh_policy: Pinned snapshot. CARTA re-acquires only when a Copernicus DEM release changes the western Pyrenean tiles, or when a proof needs an extent these six tiles do not cover. Terrain is context, not a live feed, so there is no scheduled refresh.

datasets.geographic_meaning: Ordinary geographic presentation context including countries, cities, roads, rivers, coasts, borders, and physical labels; not CARTA wine-domain authority

semantic_distinctions: Wine-region labels are derived CARTA orientation points, not statutory polygons.
INAO areas are cartographic representations of regulatory geographical areas, not parcel eligibility or actual vineyard land.
Eligible communes, approved viticultural parcels, actual vineyard land, cadastral parcels, and lieux-dits remain distinct concepts.
External sourced geography may be displayed without becoming a native CARTA guide or subject.
Terrain is context before it is interpretation: relief, slope or elevation shown on the map never authorises a claim about grape growing, ripening, drainage, climate or wine quality.
